rationale: Block 5 covers POP cast application procedure; tests the joint-above-and-below immobilisation rule, a critical safety principle examined clinically
Block 9 covers post-application assessment and complications including tight cast and compartment syndrome; tests the split/bivalve response to a tight cast

Block 6 covers Thomas splint application; tests the specific indication (femoral shaft fracture), which is a common exam trap — students may incorrectly believe it is used for tibial or other lower-limb fractures
Block 5 covers bladder catheterisation in trauma; tests the absolute contraindication of blood at urethral meatus, a high-yield safety trap that distinguishes safe practitioners
Block 3 covers the ATLS ABCDE framework; tests correct sequencing when a trauma patient's airway and breathing are intact but there is active haemorrhage — applying the priority order
Block 12 covers interpretation of resuscitation response and monitoring; tests understanding of urine output as a marker of adequate fluid resuscitation in trauma
